Subject: TTFT & streaming handshake — follow-up and demo prep

Thanks again for the call this morning, Amit — good discussion. Short recap + proposed next steps so we can line up an engineering demo and pilot: 

Summary of what PayFlux cares about
- Mobile-first users on variable networks (carrier / 3G/4G fallbacks).
- Tight perceived latency: marketing wants responses to feel near-instant on the app.
- Support for streaming incremental tokens to render partial answers while generation continues.

What we proposed on the call
- Target TTFT (time-to-first-token) for the pilot: p95 <= 150 ms (we offered this as an aggressive goal; engineering input needed).
- Streaming options: SSE preferred for broad mobile compatibility; WebSocket acceptable if you want bi-directional.
- Chunk cadence: suggested initial cadence of 150–300 ms between chunks to balance UX and tokenization overhead.
- Concurrency/throughput: need estimate from your side for concurrent active users and peak QPS.

Action items (proposed)
1) Amit: confirm expected concurrency/peak QPS and average token count per response (see questions inline).
2) Ben/SEs: propose concrete pilot SLOs and integration checklist — we suggested a lightweight demonstration of the SSE handshake and a small load run.
3) Schedule: propose Wed 11/10 or Thu 11/11 for a 45m demo + integration planning.

Attachments: attaching a simple "TTFT target matrix" (spreadsheet) that maps target SLOs to suggested batching/caching knobs. Also included a small diagram of SSE vs WS handshake we referenced.

Amit — quick answers to the questions below will help Ben size the demo environment. If it's easier, feel free to reply with a quick doc or numbers.

Key questions for sizing
- Expected active concurrent users during pilot peak: (e.g., 20, 50, 200)
- Expected average tokens per response (approx): (e.g., 40–120)
- Peak requests per second you want us to simulate for the pilot
- Any corporate network middleboxes (proxies/timeouts) we should know about that could break long-lived SSE/WS connections

Thanks — I can run the demo coordination and calendar invites.

Thanks, Irene — solid summary. A few specifics from our side: 

1) Network/profile notes
- Majority of our users are on mobile; we expect a decent fraction on flaky 4G/3G. Long-lived HTTP connections are OK but some carriers have 30–60s idle timeouts; keep that in mind for SSE.

2) Preference and cadence
- Preference: SSE for simplicity (server->client streaming) to start. We may consider WebSocket later for interactive flows.
- Cadence: our UX team likes visible incremental updates; target chunks around every 200–300 ms if possible. We understand high-frequency micro-chunks increase load.

3) Pilot sizing numbers
- Expected peak concurrent active users in pilot: ~50 (mobile active sessions generating requests intermittently).
- Average tokens per user response: ~80 tokens (typical summary payload).
- Peak QPS to simulate: ~40 requests/sec sustained for short bursts (60–90s).

4) Constraints
- Corporate proxy: our enterprise customers use proxies but for the pilot we will be testing on production mobile builds without extra corporate proxies.
- Security: we require TLS, and all connections must pass our app-level certificate pinning.

We're comfortable with a pilot that aims for p95 TTFT in the 150–250 ms range if that's realistic, but we'd like to understand the tradeoffs Ben will outline. Wed 11/10 works for a demo; 11/11 is a fallback.

— Amit Shah
Head of Product Engineering | PayFlux Solutions

Amit — great details, this is exactly what we need. Short engineering readout + recommended pilot configuration below.

High-level tradeoffs
- TTFT target: hitting p95 <= 150 ms on mobile with variable networks is challenging but achievable in many cases if:
  * model size and sequence lengths are moderate (we'll need token counts),
  * you accept a single-token initial chunk vs batching the first N tokens, and
  * we use prefix caching and warm-up routing to local replicas where possible.
- SSE vs WebSocket: SSE has simpler client compatibility and lower handshake overhead for uni-directional streaming. WebSocket gives slightly lower per-message overhead and better backpressure handling if you need client->server signals mid-generation.

Ben's recommended pilot baseline (what we'll demo)
- TTFT SLO: p95 <= 200 ms (pilot), target p95 150 ms post-optimization.
- Chunk cadence: initial demo will stream the first token as soon as available and then emit subsequent chunks every ~200–250 ms where tokens accumulate; that maps to your UX ask.
- Concurrency/throughput config for pilot: provision nodes to handle 60 QPS sustained with 50 concurrent active users and headroom for 1.5x bursts.
- Batching & caching: enable micro-batching (adaptive) with a 12 ms aggregation window; enable KV prefix caching on common prompts for faster first-token on repeated flows.

Questions we still need from PayFlux (please confirm)
- Do you want the demo to show SSE only or both SSE + WebSocket variations?
- Can you confirm 80 average tokens per response and the 40 QPS peak for the pilot?
- Any hard SLOs for p50/p95/p99 you'd like reported during the pilot? We can publish those in the dashboard.

Proposed demo agenda (45m)
- 5m intro and success criteria (Irene)
- 10m short architecture overview (Ben) — SSE handshake, routing, caching
- 15m live demo — sample mobile client (SSE) connecting to a Redwood staging endpoint, live TTFT measurements and chunk cadence
- 10m load run — short 60s burst at target QPS to show metrics and tail behavior
- 5m next steps and pilot kickoff plan

I'll attach the TTFT target matrix we referenced (spreadsheet) and the handshake diagram. We can iterate configuration after we see actual results.

If everyone is good, I'll schedule Wed 11/10 10:00–10:45 PT for the demo.
